findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the get_parent_map / hasattr interaction explicitly: either (a) IMPLEMENT get_parent_map against DC REST v2 offset pagination (preferred — the AC already requires it), or (b) if declining, OMIT the method entirely (so `hasattr` returns False and the block is silently skipped) rather than raising NotImplementedError (which passes hasattr and logs a WARNING on every fetch pass) — and update the 'never simply absent' principle to carve out hasattr-gated methods.
evidence: Plan Approach step 2: 'Where a method is genuinely not applicable to DC, it must raise a clear NotImplementedError naming the DC limitation — never be left absent'
fetcher.py:447: `if project_key and hasattr(client, 'get_parent_map'):`
fetcher.py:475: `except Exception as exc:  # BLE001 — fail-open: skip parent enrichment, write degraded snapshot` — this catches NotImplementedError

If get_parent_map is ABSENT, hasattr returns False and the block is silently skipped (zero log output). If get_parent_map raises NotImplementedError, hasattr returns True, the block executes, NotImplementedError is caught, and a WARNING is emitted on every pass.
findings.finding: The plan's 'never simply absent — always raise NotImplementedError' principle conflicts with the hasattr-gated call site for get_parent_map. fetcher.py:447 gates the call behind `hasattr(client, 'get_parent_map')`. If the DC transport declares the method but raises NotImplementedError, hasattr returns True (method exists), the block executes, and the NotImplementedError propagates into the outer `except Exception` at fetcher.py:475 — which logs a WARNING on every single reconcile fetch pass for the lifetime of a DC deployment. Conversely, omitting the method entirely makes hasattr return False and silently skips the block with no log noise. The plan mandates NotImplementedError for all 'not applicable' verdicts without noting that the hasattr gate makes omission the less-noisy choice for this specific method.
findings.location: Approach section step 2 / fetcher.py:447-480 / Acceptance Criteria: get_parent_map bullet

Every operator looking at DC reconcile logs sees this warning permanently, suggesting a degraded state rather than a deliberate capability boundary.
Alternative: get_parent_map is IMPLEMENTED for DC (v2 offset pagination per the AC) — in which case the conflict disappears entirely and is the preferred outcome per the plan's AC.

findings.finding: The DC transport has no raw HTTP request infrastructure (no `_direct_rest_get`, `_direct_rest_put_raw`, `_direct_rest_post_json` equivalents), yet the plan instructs implementing `set_entity_property`, `set_issue_property`, `get_issue_by_rest`, and `validate_assignee_exists` 'against DC's REST v2 API' without specifying whether to (a) add urllib helpers to `JiraDataCenterTransport`, (b) use pycontribs' internal `_session`, or (c) use pycontribs native methods. If implementers choose raw HTTP they must add significant new infrastructure; if they choose pycontribs methods they must first verify those methods exist. The plan is silent on this architectural choice, which is load-bearing for every 'IMPLEMENT' verdict in the triage.

Without this requirement, an implementer may defensively wrap a method body in a broad `try/except`, silently reproducing exactly the swallowing problem the plan criticises in existing code. The plan's own framing shows this risk is real: 7 of 12 methods are 'swallowed at EVERY site' by callers, so it is already a default reflex in this codebase.

evidence: Acceptance criteria list 13 bullet points; none mention logging, metrics, or alerting for new transport methods
'Seven members whose call sites swallow Exception at every site' — if the transport also fails silently, the failure is completely invisible
Approach step 1 discusses REST contract; step 2 discusses NotImplementedError; neither mentions instrumentation
Testing section covers unit and structural tests but not observability assertions
findings.finding: The plan adds up to twelve new external REST call sites on the DC transport but specifies no observability requirement (logging, metrics, or tracing) for those new failure points. When a newly implemented method fails in a live DC deployment, operators have no specified mechanism to detect or diagnose the failure — particularly dangerous for the seven methods whose callers already swallow exceptions, where a REST failure at the transport layer would be invisible even in logs unless the transport itself emits one.
findings.location: Approach section; Scope section (transport.py); Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: `get_parent_map` silently returns an empty result because DC returns a 503; the reconciler skips parent assignment; no log line is emitted; operators see 'converged' in the run summary.
`delete_issue` fails with a 403 (permission error); the swallowing caller masks it; no metric or alert fires; links accumulate indefinitely.
